prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: RTL · صفوف معنونة (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 4 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "البند" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 151px
  col 2: header "الربع الأول" · longest unbreakable word 26px · one-line width 54px
  col 3: header "الربع الثاني" · longest unbreakable word 30px · one-line width 58px
  col 4: header "ملاحظات" · longest unbreakable word 52px · one-line width 384px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 453px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 452px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"The quarter columns are clear and comparable, but the long note wraps into four lines while the row-header column has spare space."},"B":{"grade":"poor","why":"Both the row labels and the long note wrap heavily, making the first two rows tall; the quarter columns have disproportionate spare space."},"C":{"grade":"excellent","why":"The row labels remain easy to scan, the quarter headers and values align clearly, and the wider notes column gives the long note a comfortable three-line shape."},"D":{"grade":"good","why":"The long note reads comfortably in two lines, but both quarter headers wrap, weakening the compact comparison between those columns."},"E":{"grade":"excellent","why":"The columns are well balanced: quarter headers stay on one line, row labels are readable, and the long note forms a compact three-line block."},"F":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"The row labels fit on one line, but the oversized label column leaves the long note in a narrow, five-line stack."}},"best":["C","E"],"confidence":"high","unsure":"C and E are very close; their small difference in column proportions does not clearly favor one."}
